stip.intro: Each of the 1,000 selected students is given a stipend of ₹10,000 for the one-month internship. It is paid by bank transfer to the student's own bank account. The selected students give their bank details in the candidate portal, in the steps below.

stip.s1: Only the students of the final selected list give bank details. The merit list is published on this portal, and the application status page shows your result.

stip.need_account: the account number and the IFSC (11 characters), as printed in your passbook or cheque book

stip.s3: Sign in to the candidate portal with your application number, your date of birth and the last four digits of your mobile number, and open this page:
stip.s4_t: Fill in the form and send it
stip.s4: Type every entry in English letters (A-Z) and digits, as printed in your passbook. Type the account number twice. Upload the proof, read and tick the three declarations, and send the form before the last date.
stip.s5: Once sent, the details cannot be changed. CICT checks them against your proof. If something is wrong, CICT returns them with a note on the same page: correct them and send them again. Look at the page from time to time.
stip.s6: When the details are approved, the stipend is paid by bank transfer into that account. The page then shows that it is paid, with the date and the payment reference.

home.j1: Twelve delegations from Tamil Nadu travelled to Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya in the first month-long Sangamam, hosted at Banaras Hindu University.
home.j2: Academic and cultural sessions at Namo Ghat, with the first real-time Tamil translation of the Prime Minister's address.
home.j3: The legacy of Sage Agasthyar and Indian knowledge traditions; 1,200 participants, including students from central universities.
home.j4: “Let us learn Tamil”: Tamil teachers in the schools of Varanasi, a study tour of Tamil Nadu, and the Agasthya Expedition from Tenkasi to Kashi.
about.lead: Kashi Tamil Sangamam celebrates the civilisational bond between Tamil Nadu and Kashi. It was conceived as an expression of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat: two of India's oldest centres of learning, Kashi on the Ganga and the Tamil country on the Vaigai and the Kaveri, meeting to rediscover shared traditions of language, scholarship, faith, craft and cuisine.
about.p1: KTS 5.0 takes the Thirukkural, the 1,330 couplets of Thiruvalluvar, as its unifying theme. The couplets speak of virtue, wealth and love in a language that every Indian tradition recognises as its own, which is why the Central Institute of Classical Tamil has translated the text into all twenty-two languages of the Eighth Schedule.
about.p2: Under this theme, one thousand participating institutions across India each assess their students on the Thirukkural and select one; the thousand selected students study the Thirukkural through a ten-lecture orientation in their own language, write a research paper, and then carry the text back to their campuses through presentations of their own.
about.who1: The Ministry of Education is the nodal ministry for the Sangamam.
about.who2: The Central Institute of Classical Tamil, Chennai, implements KTS 5.0: this portal, registration and selection, the multilingual orientation, the digital repository, apps, films, publications and outreach to schools.
about.who3: IIT Madras and Banaras Hindu University are the nodal and coordinating institutes on the Tamil Nadu side and the Kashi side.
about.who4: Indian Railways, the Airports Authority of India, the National Highways Authority of India, the Ministry of Culture, UGC, AICTE, CBSE, KVS and the Governments of Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh are partners for displays, outreach, travel and venues.
about.caption: Thiruvalluvar, author of the Thirukkural
about.j1: More than 2,500 people from Tamil Nadu, from twelve walks of life, visited Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya on eight-day tours. Organised by the Ministry of Education with the Government of Uttar Pradesh at Banaras Hindu University.
about.j2: Held at Namo Ghat, Varanasi, with interactive academic sessions between professionals from Tamil Nadu and Kashi, and real-time Tamil translation of the inaugural address through an app.
about.j3: Bridging Indian knowledge and tradition with contemporary discourse, and highlighting the legacy of Sage Agasthyar; 1,200 participants, including 200 students of Tamil origin from central universities.
about.j4: “Let us learn Tamil”: fifty Tamil teachers taught in the schools of Varanasi, 300 students from Varanasi studied Tamil in colleges in Tamil Nadu, and the Agasthya Expedition travelled from Tenkasi to Kashi. The valedictory function was held at Rameswaram.
about.j5: “Thirukkural Payilvom”: the Thirukkural for every campus in India, in every Indian language.
prog.part2: Apps, videos, films, conferences and public displays
prog.part3: Reaching students who do not speak Tamil
prog.i1.d: This website: a single place for programme administration, participant registration, content delivery and coordination among the participating agencies. It carries the registration and selection system, the candidate portal with the online test, the digital repository and the coordination hub of the partners.
prog.i2.d: A fully accessible repository of learning materials and research assets: the Thirukkural in the Indian languages and in foreign languages, research publications, the Thirukkural Multilingual App, the Thirukkural Ground-Truth Corpus of palm-leaf manuscripts, and related websites.
prog.i3.d: A campaign across India, through the Nodal Institutions of the States/UTs, academic institutions, digital media and partner universities, brings 1,000 participating institutions to the programme. The institutions register on this portal, assess their students and register the student each has selected.
prog.i3.l2: Eligibility: students currently enrolled in any college or university in India
prog.i4.d: Each participating institution assesses its students on the Thirukkural, by the online test that the portal offers in the language each student chose or by any other suitable mode, and selects one student on merit. CICT consolidates the selected students, with State-wise and language-wise representation, into the list of 1,000 student delegates, one from each institution.
prog.i5.d: A ten-part series of academic video lectures on the Thirukkural, offered in the 22 scheduled languages, Tamil among them, and in English (23 languages in all): translated, dubbed or subtitled, delivered language by language, with a 20-minute live question-and-answer segment in each session.
prog.i6.d: All 1,000 selected students undertake a one-month internship, and each of them will be given a stipend of ₹10,000, to deepen their understanding of the Thirukkural, its values, its philosophy and its relevance today.
prog.i7.t: Student presentation and dissemination of knowledge
prog.i7.d: Every delegate is prepared to deliver a one-hour presentation or lecture on the Thirukkural in his or her own college, under the guidance of a designated faculty mentor, so that each of the 1,000 campuses hears the couplets from one of its own students.
prog.a1.d: All 1,330 couplets with the translations of CICT into the 22 scheduled languages, two Tamil commentaries, English prose, word-level grammar, metrical analysis and references to palm-leaf manuscripts. It works offline, carries no advertisements, and is released under the CC BY 4.0 licence.
prog.a2.d: Twenty-minute lectures on selected couplets in Indian languages, explaining their meaning, values and relevance, published on the YouTube channels of CICT and on this portal.
prog.a3.d: Recitations of the couplets with meanings, explanations and translations in several languages, designed for visually impaired students, for those who learn by listening, and for audiences who do not know Tamil.
prog.a4.d: Recitation of the entire text, couplet by couplet, with the Tamil commentary of Dr Mu. Varadarajan, for correct pronunciation and for the study of the three sections.
prog.a5.d: Fifteen-minute films that dramatise selected couplets on ethical leadership, social harmony, truthfulness, gratitude and civic duty, screened at KTS venues, on campuses and by broadcasters.
prog.a6.d: Animated videos of sixty to ninety seconds on individual couplets, made with the help of artificial intelligence, with subtitles in many languages, published every day on the social media channels of CICT.
prog.a7.t: Annual National Conference on the Thirukkural
prog.a7.d: Held in major cities with the Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti and Banaras Hindu University, bringing together scholars and translators from every language region.
prog.a8.d: Couplets with translations on passenger information systems and signboards at railway stations, airports and highway toll plazas, in coordination with Indian Railways, the Airports Authority of India and the National Highways Authority of India.
prog.a9.d: Illustrated stories for children inspired by the Thirukkural, first in English and Hindi, distributed through school boards and available for download from this portal.
prog.a10.d: Print-ready posters in many languages for schools, colleges and libraries, distributed to CBSE, KVS, JNV and state school networks, and available for download.
prog.b1.d: A calendar of couplets for 200 school days, one for each morning assembly, with the translation and meaning in the language of the school, distributed as printed flip-charts and as digital packages.
prog.b2.d: Collections of scripts, guides to narration and ideas for the stage, so that students present the values of the Thirukkural through stories, speeches, skits, plays and dance-dramas.
prog.b3.d: Crosswords, puzzles, complete-the-line games, memory pairs, word-guessing and typing challenges, with interfaces in many languages and levels from beginner to scholar.

nodal.intro: The Nodal Higher Educational Institution of each State/UT identifies the participating institutions of its State/UT, ensures that they register on this portal, and coordinates their assessments, nominations and campus activities.
nodal.how_title: How the programme reaches the institutions
nodal.p1: In view of its standing and coordinating capacity, one higher educational institution in each State or Union Territory is designated as the Nodal Higher Educational Institution. It identifies up to 50 higher educational institutions within its State or Union Territory and coordinates their participation, with due regard to geographical spread and institutional representation. It nominates a senior officer as the State/UT Nodal Officer, forwards the list of institutions identified, coordinates nomination and registration, facilitates the qualifying examination and the orientation, and monitors the timely completion of the activities.
nodal.p2: Each participating institution assesses its interested students on the Thirukkural, selects one student on merit and nominates them with one Faculty Supervisor/Guide. The nomination is endorsed by the Director, Registrar, Principal or Head of the Institution, and the institution registers the selected student on this portal.
nodal.p3: On the basis of the institution-level assessments and the prescribed selection process, 1,000 students are selected, with appropriate State-wise and language-wise representation.
nodal.p4: Participating institutions may also organise academic and cultural activities based on the Thirukkural, such as essay writing, quizzes, debates, elocution, recitation, storytelling, poster-making and presentations, for wider student engagement. A brief report on the activities undertaken is submitted to CICT and the Ministry in the prescribed format.

hei.intro: The higher educational institutions taking part in KTS 5.0 – Thirukkural Payilvom, State/UT by State/UT, identified by the Nodal Institution of each State/UT. Each of them assesses its students, selects one on merit and registers the selected student on this portal, with a Faculty Supervisor/Guide, endorsed by the Head of the Institution.
hei.empty: No institution has been accepted yet.
hei.reg_intro: Higher educational institutions identified by the Nodal Institution of their State/UT register here to take part in KTS 5.0; any other institution may apply, and the Nodal Officer of the State/UT reviews the application. A participating institution is listed on this portal, assesses its students (the portal offers a ready online test), selects one on merit and registers the selected student here.
hei.english_note: Fill in this form in English: write the names in English letters (A-Z).
hei.coord_help: The member of the faculty who coordinates the participation of the institution: the portal writes to this email address, and the coordinator signs in to the institution's page with it.
hei.guide_help: The member of the faculty nominated, with the approval of the Head of the Institution, to guide the selected student's study of the Thirukkural, the research paper and the presentation. The portal fills these details in the registration of the selected student.
